Hackers use old Bitly links to re-direct to offensive content

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (528 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media.
  • That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.
  • Link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media. According to the service provider Bitly, its hyperlinks in older tweets from many companies, politicians, and even government accounts are now redirecting to “content unrelated to the original posts.”.

That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.

Link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds. The service typically works by pinning a website’s lengthy, complex URL address to a tidied-up, abbreviated shortcut in a digital registry. This shortened address then redirects anyone who clicks it to their intended online destination.

Industry observers note that well…in theory. Security analysts have tried to warn people about an concern known as “bit rot” for decades. In 2009—about one year after Bitly’s debut—Silicon Valley entrepreneur Joshua Schacter wrote a prescient blog post cautioning against what he felt were potentially serious flaws in the link-shortening “middleman” system. Amid the issues, Schacter cited a “latest and potentially unreliable” tool that ties an original hyperlink to the “health of a third party.”.

“The shortener may decide a link is a Terms Of Service violation and delete it. If the shortener accidentally erases a database, forgets to renew its domain, or just disappears, the link will break,” he explained. “If a top-level domain changes its policy on commercial use, the link will break. If the shortener gets hacked, every link becomes a potential phishing attack.”.

It now appears bad actors recently identified countless of these Bitly links previously posted across social media between 2009 and 2014. Although their exact methods aren’t clear, it’s possible they generated their own custom Bitly links using the addresses in the social media posts, then used those to send people to different destinations. Bitly says its links do not automatically expire, but paid users may redirect existing links.

Many examples were found among the more than 60,000 posts on X from President Donald Trump’s official account. In one of Trump’s previous posts about his golf course in Scotland, the Bitly link temporarily redirected to Wikipedia’s entry on the Epstein Files. Targets also included corporations like McDonald’s, with one of the fast food giant’s 2011 Bitly URLs suddenly linked to Wikipedia’s page about the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Not every hijacked post funneled people to upsetting outcomes. Instead of a cybersecurity PSA, the Bitly address in a 2021 post from the FBI briefly linked to a photo of a blubbery seal. Another of Trump’s URLs sent you to the popular video game, Geometry Dash.

In its acknowledgement of the problem on November 15, Bitly reported it had identified and suspended the bad actors’ accounts, and were in the process of “disabling the affected links.”.

“Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the issue and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote at the time.

#86911. Can AI Companions Really Help Us Feel Less Lonely?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (998 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Can AI Companions Really Help Us Feel Less Lonely?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • As more and more people turn to artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT for a wide range of applications, researchers are now asking whether the digital relationships they can provide might also meet our need for social connection.
  • Sources indicate that for most of us, simple friendship is having someone to talk to, share experiences with, and turn to when things go wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

As more and more people turn to artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT for a wide range of applications, researchers are now asking whether the digital relationships they can provide might also meet our need for social connection.

Sources indicate that for most of us, simple friendship is having someone to talk to, share experiences with, and turn to when things go wrong. Whether this friendship has endured for decades or involves someone we met recently, having a social connection can be invaluable, even as we grow older and more isolated. But what if the “friend” isn't actually human? Since the introduction of large language models and conversational artificial intelligence, ChatGPT and other services have become part of everyday life. Millions of people have already turned to AI chatbots for answering basic questions about everything from financial planning to medical concerns. Many people also ask for help with personal problems and look to these tools for emotional support and companionship.

Certainly, AI chatbots offer advantages when human contact is unavailable. They're available anytime, day or night, and you don't have to set up a meeting, worry about interrupting, or fear being judged for any personal confessions you make. Users can also keep talking for as long as they want without worrying that the chatbot will end the session early.

In a recent development, for people dealing with loneliness, this kind of care can be a tremendous source of comfort. But could having an AI pal make loneliness worse? This is a worry, especially for people dealing with psychological issues that require professional (human) help. An article recently published in the journal Translational Issues in Psychological Science addresses many concerns about social chatbots. In the article, researchers Zehra Merve Kaya and Edanur Kanbur at Boğaziçi University in Turkey present results from numerous studies into artificial companionship and how it can function as an alternative to the human social relationships we depend on. They conclude that artificial companions can help reduce loneliness, but only temporarily and to a limited extent.

In a recent development, loneliness is much more than simply being alone. Many people enjoy solitude without feeling lonely; others may have extensive social connections but still feel their emotional needs aren’t being met. For them, having numerous friends, supportive families, and an active social life might still leave them feeling incomplete. Ultimately, loneliness is defined by the gap between perceived and desired social bonds. And it is far more common than you might think. According to a 2025 WHO report, one in six people surveyed globally reported feeling lonely, often for long periods. Being chronically lonely has been associated with medical and psychological problems, including depression, heart disease, cognitive decline, and premature death. Though most commonly associated with old age, loneliness can strike at any age. Surveys of adolescents and young adults suggest high levels of loneliness, despite social media and other online communication.

So, can artificial intelligence make a difference? Modern chatbots can display empathic statements, handle personal disclosures, ask follow-up questions, and otherwise respond in ways that mimic social contact and make lonely people feel heard and understood. Along with always being available, AI chatbots can also provide someone to talk to during a sleepless evening. People dealing with social anxiety can often view chatbots as a way of avoiding many problems with human connection. That includes the fear of embarrassment and rejection, as well as building a sense of trust. Still, when you interact with a (live) friend, your shared experiences often shape their response to a cry for help. That includes memories, emotions, and your shared understanding of your joint connection. Even when the friend doesn’t know what to say, that concern still comes through, along with the sense of being acknowledged by someone with their own ideas, feelings, and wants. Relationships are based on shared experience, disagreement, compromise, and trust.

It has been revealed that AI works differently, however. While a very empathetic chatbot might respond to someone’s fears or even offer helpful tips, no human hears the user’s feelings. Instead, AI provides an online system trained to recognize patterns and deliver relevant language. Though it may seem real to many people in distress, no AI system today can mimic the qualities of friendship that a human can provide (yet).There are also practical concerns related to talking with chatbots, because they can save and use sensitive data without the user’s knowledge. Providing chatbots as psychological support agents means having to resolve complications of privacy, informed consent, and emotional dependency.

AI is changing rapidly. Chatbots have evolved to extended, natural conversations, and future versions may become even better at memorizing personal details, responding to emotions, and adapting to humans. Whether this technology helps with loneliness or creates other problems remains unclear. Kaya and Kanbur note that most of the evidence they have presented has not yielded clear results (thus far). While AI companionship can help many people, too many questions remain unanswered to recommend it as a widespread option.

Sources indicate that true friendship is more than talking with a perpetually upbeat companion that may not really understand what you are saying. We also need to form ties with others with various lives and experiences that may challenge our perspective. These relationships matter because they require effort to maintain.

While artificial intelligence can imitate many qualities of companionship convincingly, it cannot form an emotional bond. That is what makes human relationships unique. Ultimately, artificial intelligence is not a substitute for human contact, though it may work as a helper in the short term. Whether it cures loneliness or keeps people apart is still an open question.

Sources indicate that kaya, Z. M., & Kanbur, E. (2026). Artificial intelligence as a social substitute in loneliness. Translational Problems in Psychological Science. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1037/tps0000547.

Being stranded at the airport is no fun. You can only eat so many Auntie Anne's pretzels and play Candy Crush for so long; eventually, you need to get to your destination. But what if that destination is 1600 miles away, every flight in the country is grounded, and there are no rental cars or trains available?

Well, you could take an Uber to a local Ford dealership and drop $48,000 on a newly introduced Ford Bronco. And according to a report from NBC News, that is exactly what Tara Harding did.

In a recent development, according to NBC, Harding and two of her employees were in Charlotte, North Carolina for training, and were set to fly back home to Bismarck, North Dakota last Friday. That is, until the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grounded all flights across the country. Thousands of flights were cancelled or delayed as a result.

Recent findings suggest that the three women began to look at alternate transportation options, but none of them had any luck. There were no rental cars, buses, trains, or ride shares that could get them home. They were stuck in Charlotte. Harding called her husband to let him know, which is when her mother-in-law made a suggestion: “Why don’t you guys go buy a car?”.

Recent findings suggest that harding decided to investigate that possibility. Being what she described to NBC as a self-proclaimed “Ford girl,” Harding texted a local Ford dealer. The salesman mentioned he would wait until the women arrived, which they did around 7:45 pm. Two hours and $48,000 later, Harding was the proud owner of a upcoming Ford Bronco. The road trip was on.

Sources indicate that harding is a nurse practitioner, and she owns her own clinic; she had patients scheduled for Monday, and she remarked she wanted to get her employees back home to their family. So, they covered the 1600 miles by driving 27 hours straight. The women took turns behind the wheel, sleeping while the others drove, while gas stations and drive-thrus provided the necessary fuel for both the Bronco and its occupants.

Recent findings suggest that originally, Harding mentioned she planned to sell the Bronco once she got home. However, she added that while she was catching up on sleep, her husband took it for three drives and decided he wanted to keep it. So, the nationwide flight may have cost Harding $48,000—but at least she now has a cool newly introduced Bronco, and one heck of a story to tell.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This new food pyramid emphasizes plant-based protein sources, cooking with plant-based oils, and healthier sugars and carbohydrates.
  • It also echoes the traditional food pyramid used in the United States since 1992.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A first-of-its-kind international food pyramid, developed by 22 leading nutritionists from Europe, Canada, the United States, and Australia, was published in Advances in Nutrition in September.

This new food pyramid emphasizes plant-based protein sources, cooking with plant-based oils, and healthier sugars and carbohydrates.

It also echoes the traditional food pyramid used in the United States since 1992.

It has been revealed that the upcoming pyramid breaks away from the Trump administration’s updated nutritional guidelines, which are part of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Health Again (MAHA) agenda and prioritize red meat over plants.

The new pyramid was designed by a research team led by Brigham Young University professor Karen Della Corte. The researchers noted that this is the first international food pyramid that is designed to reflect scientific agreement across multiple countries and cultures.

Della Corte and researchers from the International Carbohydrate Quality Consortium (ICQC), compared dietary guidelines from multiple countries, including:.

They also analyzed evidence from more than 250 scientific publications, while drawing on the EAT-Lancet Planetary Health Diet to identify principles of healthy eating that may be shared.

The newly introduced pyramid highlights three guidelines:.

While the pyramid emphasizes plant-based proteins, it doesn’t exclude animal proteins.

“I find the latest international food pyramid a more practical and aligned approach for the prevention of chronic disease,” said Michelle Routhenstein, Preventive Cardiology Dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the creation of the food pyramid.

“The fresh international food pyramid places greater emphasis on food quality and the importance of building meals around nutrient-dense plant foods, while still allowing room for lean animal proteins such as fish, poultry, eggs, and yogurt,” she added.

While the new pyramid and the current U.S. dietary guidelines differ in many ways, they also agree on certain factors.

For example, both sets of guidelines discourage added sugars, refined carbs, and highly processed snacks.

The differences between the two mainly lie in their emphasis on specific sources of protein and fat. For example, the newly introduced pyramid prioritizes plant-based proteins, while the U.S. guidelines place greater emphasis on animal proteins, including red meat.

While both sets of recommendations advise limiting saturated fat, the fresh pyramid emphasizes unsaturated plant oils, whereas the U.S. guidelines also include butter and beef tallow as cooking fat options.

Sources indicate that routhenstein noted that an crucial distinction is that this upcoming pyramid goes beyond simply telling people to eat more protein or fewer carbohydrates. Instead, it encourages people to consider the quality and sources of those nutrients.

However, the main emphasis of both guidelines is encouraging people to eat fewer ultra-processed foods and more natural or “real” foods.

Routhenstein told Healthline that research consistently indicates that plant-forward eating patterns, including the Mediterranean and DASH diets, are associated with better cardiovascular health and a lower risk of heart disease.

Plant foods provide fiber, potassium, antioxidants, and other beneficial compounds that can help support healthy cholesterol levels, blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood vessel function.

“This is not to say that protein and fat are unimportant, but their sources matter,” Routhenstein said.

In a statement from BYU, Della Corte shared the following tips for incorporating the newly introduced pyramid’s recommendations into your diet:.

It has been revealed that the pyramid is a framework, not a personalized prescription. If you have questions about your individual nutritional needs, you can speak with your healthcare professional or a licensed dietitian.

Recent findings suggest that “It is important to recognize that plant-forward does not mean vegan or vegetarian. The amount and sources of animal protein should be considered to ensure they align with an individual’s cardiometabolic goals and lab targets,” Routhenstein remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that around the world, the number of uncontacted Indigenous tribes continues to dwindle. Indigenous rights advocates estimate that half of the nearly 200 communities still existing in comparative isolation could disappear within a decade, without proper safeguards against climate change, land loss, fame-seeking opportunists, and illegal industrial encroachments. Unfortunately, the situation has apparently grown so dire that some Indigenous groups are reaching out for help—and exposing themselves to potentially deadly foreign diseases in the process.

Recent findings suggest that on November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon. Although proficient hunter-gatherers, the group requested yams before taking them back into the rainforest.

“This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger,” Survival International director Caroline Pearce stated in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that the Awá are one of the world’s last uncontacted Indigenous tribes, whose ties to the Brazilian rainforest stretch back centuries. They faced their first attacks from European settlers during the 1800s, which eventually forced them to adopt a nomadic lifestyle to avoid future encounters. Brazil finally supplied the Awá with settlement areas during the mid-1980s, but it still took years before the government properly invested in demarcated land. In the meantime, numerous deadly interactions with loggers, farmers, and other illegal intruders had reduced the Awá community to barely 300 people. Of those, advocates estimate only about one-third of the hunter-gatherers remain completely isolated from the outside world.

“The Brazilian government must commit the resources necessary to protect [the region of] Arariboia from the loggers and ranchers who are razing it, in flagrant defiance of the law,” Pearce added.

According to recent reports, in addition to the advocacy work by Survival International, the Awá are supported by a team of Indigenous members of the Guajajara community known as the Forest Guardians. These volunteers have spent years pushing back against illegal cattle ranchers and loggers attempting to claim land in Arariboia, often dying as a result of their efforts.

It has been revealed that “The Forest Guardians have always worked to protect the Awá against encroachment, even at the cost of losing warriors in battle,” the organization remarked. “We demand immediate action from the relevant authorities…to ensure what the Awá believe is best for them, safeguarding their lives, health, safety and dignity. FOR THE AWÁ, FOR THE TENETEHAR [language], AND FOR THE FOREST!”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit.
  • Sources indicate that it’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027.
  • Sources indicate that enhancement: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center looks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit. Tesla rates it at 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuously at 34.5 kV, with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA of peak power.

Sources indicate that it’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027. That’s the same year Heron Power, the startup founded by Tesla’s former top engineer Drew Baglino, plans to start volume production of its own solid-state transformer, the Heron Link.

Sources indicate that enhancement: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center looks. We’ve updated the article with the new details.

Recent findings suggest that tesla first said it would build its own transformers in September 2025, when it unveiled Megapack 3 and Megablock. Megablock connects four Megapack 3 units to a transformer and switchgear, but Tesla shared next to nothing about the transformer itself.

Powercore is that missing piece. Tesla unveiled it today through its Tesla Megapack account on X:.

Introducing PowercoreSolid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak powerMade in America. Operating 2027 pic.twitter.com/sHxqnpWJrf.

About an hour later, Tesla followed up with a much longer post on X laying out the full spec sheet:.

In a recent development, it also packs a built-in solid-state medium-voltage breaker that Tesla says clears faults up to 1,000x faster than a conventional breaker. There’s no flammable oil, and it’s modular, so components can be serviced in the field without swapping the whole unit.

According to recent reports, tesla is pitching one product for three markets: battery storage, utility-scale solar, and 800 Vdc data centers. For Megablock, Powercore replaces the current two-step setup, where Megapack’s inverters output 480 V AC before a separate transformer steps it up to medium voltage. Tesla says that old architecture had twice the losses. For solar, Powercore works as a central inverter for today’s 1,500 Vdc arrays and upcoming 2,000 Vdc systems.

Recent findings suggest that tesla still hasn’t shared pricing, customers, or a factory location. It only says Powercore will be made in the US “of U.S. and imported parts” with first units operating in 2027.

According to recent reports, the idea behind a solid-state transformer is simple enough. A typical solar or battery project uses low-voltage inverters to convert DC into AC, then a major oil-filled, iron-core transformer to step that up to grid voltage. A solid-state unit does both jobs with silicon carbide power electronics, which means less gear, a smaller footprint, and active control over voltage and frequency. That control is what “grid-forming” means: the unit can help hold the grid steady instead of just following it.

And with lead times on conventional transformers stretching into years as data centers and renewable projects pile into interconnection queues, there’s real demand for an alternative.

You can’t look at Powercore without thinking of Heron Power.

In a recent development, baglino spent 18 years at Tesla and finished as SVP of powertrain and energy, in charge of batteries, motors, power electronics, and energy products. He left in April 2024 and launched Heron Power in 2025 to build solid-state transformers.

In a recent development, he brought a lot of Tesla’s power electronics talent with him. As we reported when Tesla first announced its transformer intends, Heron hired engineers who led power electronics design for Powerwall 3, the next-gen Megapack, and Superchargers, along with the person who ran Tesla’s power electronics controls team for charging and energy products.

Since then, Heron has raised a $38 million Series A, a $140 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and a $60 million credit facility from J.P. Morgan and TriplePoint Capital. Former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn sits on its board, and Tesla co-founder JB Straubel is an investor.

It has been revealed that it’s also building Heron Factory One, a 286,000-square-foot plant in Morgan Hill, California, designed to make 10,000 Heron Links a year. That’s over 40 GW of annual capacity, with commercial production planned for late 2027.

In a recent development, and the customers are lining up. Vantage reserved more than 1 GW for its data centers, Intersect reserved 1.5 GW, LG Energy Solution Vertech is integrating Heron Link with its US-made battery systems, and RWE signed a pilot to install Heron Links at a Texas battery storage site in April 2027. Baglino says Heron has 50 GW of orders in the pipeline.

Here’s how the two compare based on what each tech giant has disclosed:.

On paper, Powercore is the bigger box, and now it has the better numbers too. At 7.4 MW continuous, it carries about 50% more power per unit than the 5 MW Heron Link, and its 98.86% peak efficiency edges out Heron’s 98.6%. But Tesla’s figure is a peak number, and Heron doesn’t label its own as one, so it’s not quite apples to apples. Neither firm has shared pricing.

According to recent reports, tesla is also going straight at Heron’s data center pitch. Powercore converts medium voltage directly to 800 Vdc, the rack architecture Nvidia is pushing, and Tesla says it’s working with Nvidia on 800 Vdc designs. Heron’s data center version does the same 34.5 kV AC to 800 VDC conversion with built-in storage, and data centers make up about a third of its business. Tesla’s answer to the storage piece is Megapack on the DC bus, and it says it already has 10 GWh of Megapack running at data centers.

This one is a little awkward for Tesla.

Industry observers note that A substantial chunk of the people who designed Tesla’s power electronics over the last decade now work at Heron, and the guy who ran the whole org is its CEO. Tesla’s energy business also lost its longtime leader, Mike Snyder, last month, according to the WSJ.

This is all wrong. Tesla started developing this 3 years ago. Before Heron. The team selling Powercore is same as Megapack that has a way larger customer base than Heron. Also Heron is not a bankable manufacturer per project finance terms. So they will struggle to get projects financed through equity and senior debt . Not as Tesla.

To be fair, Tesla still has plenty of power electronics expertise. Its silicon carbide inverters are in millions of cars and every Megapack. And it has something Heron doesn’t: a massive installed base and a sales channel. Tesla says it’s almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027, and bundling Powercore into Megablock is an easy upsell. Plenty of developers will take the one-stop shop.

Tesla’s specs now match or beat Heron’s on paper. But Heron has named customers, a pilot site with an install date, and a factory under construction. Tesla has none of those yet. I wouldn’t be surprised if Heron is actually ahead here.

But either way, the transformer shortage is big enough for both companies to sell everything they can build.

The Best Way to Respond After a Fight

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.
  • In a recent development, comedian Brian Gaar has remarked, “Relationships are mostly you apologizing for saying something hilarious.” He is right that relationships involve differences about what is hilarious, and that partners need to apologize.
  • In a recent development, marriage researcher John Gottman has mentioned that some fighting couples get trapped in the roach motel, where, as the old advertisement put it, “they get in, but they can’t get out.” These relationship “disasters,” as he calls them, contrast with relationship “masters” who have figured out how to either stop, calm down, or focus on solutions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

In a recent development, comedian Brian Gaar has remarked, “Relationships are mostly you apologizing for saying something hilarious.” He is right that relationships involve differences about what is hilarious, and that partners need to apologize. People are human, with the weaknesses and differences that are part of life. Every couple gets off course at times, which can lead to each person becoming more attached to their position, resulting in a heated back-and-forth over who is correct. Proving a point can become more vital than stopping the harm that is piling up.

In a recent development, marriage researcher John Gottman has mentioned that some fighting couples get trapped in the roach motel, where, as the old advertisement put it, “they get in, but they can’t get out.” These relationship “disasters,” as he calls them, contrast with relationship “masters” who have figured out how to either stop, calm down, or focus on solutions. One therapy approach calls this ability to exit damaging situations “workability.” This is a focus on what helps, instead of worrying about who did what. It may be true that the other acted like a toddler, slamming the door and stomping feet, but it might be more workable to focus on what would improve the current mood. It may be accurate to say they were wrong in the facts about what your mother actually said, but is that helpful to argue about? Is it moving the relationship forward? In throwing out opinions about who is right and wrong, it is good to consider the old advice: Is it true? Is it kind? Is it necessary? And, is it workable? Workability does not ask, “Who is right?” but “What is the right thing to do?”.

According to recent reports, one of the most workable actions in a relationship is a repair attempt. Time will heal many wounds, but injuries heal faster with treatment. This can happen in a kind conversation that contains conciliatory efforts. One study looked directly at the power of healing gestures. People filled out questionnaires and described incidents in which they had recently been hurt. The researchers followed participants for several weeks to find out what the offender did to make things right. Some did nothing, but others apologized, made recompense, and had a peacemaking attitude. The more steps the offender took, the more the other forgave. Positive attempts changed the way that the hurt person viewed the relationship and the other. Trying to make things right is almost always a step in the right direction.

Couple therapist and researcher Sue Johnson offers guidelines for addressing injuries that are not healing on their own. First, partners should speak about the hurt honestly and simply. This should focus on the feelings, not the fault of the one who caused it. The listening partner acknowledges the pain without getting defensive or excusing themselves. Second, the injurer needs to take ownership of what they did. This needs to be done without downplaying what happened. A real apology is needed, not a "Sorrrrreeee! Sheesh!” Even if the offender doesn’t agree on every particular—and they probably won’t—it is key to not get stuck rehashing details. Instead, partners should converse about what needs to be done next. This can be done by focusing on underlying needs, such as safety, responsiveness, and connection. This will provide a sense of moving forward and is reassuring. If couples can talk through the events without getting upset, it helps rework the memory into a less bitter version.

According to recent reports, it is important to nurture and treat wounds, but that doesn’t fix things immediately. Someone can apologize profusely for breaking another’s arm, but the pain will still last for a while. The person who caused the injury has to allow this and not get frustrated: “I said I was sorry, just go use your arm already!” They also must feel regret for the pain, not just the problems it has created. Sincere apologies help couples recalibrate and commit to do better. The next time you say something hilarious but unhelpful, resist the urge to escalate. Try a sincere repair instead.

Harris, Russ, ACT with Love: Stop Struggling, Reconcile Differences, and Strengthen Your Relationship with Acceptance and Commitment (Upcoming York: New Harbinger Publications, 2009).

Industry observers note that michael E. McCullough, Eric J. Pedersen, Benjamin A. Tabak, and Evan C. Carter, "Conciliatory Gestures Promote Forgiveness and Reduce Anger in Humans," Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 111, no. 30 (2014): 11211-11216.

Sue Johnson, Hold Me Tight: Seven Conversations For A Lifetime Of Love (New York: Little, Brown, and Company, 2008).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in July, Aston Martin revealed an unconventional new vehicle called the Dreadnought. It was a digital-only, military-specification vehicle for the video game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, meant to be the ultimate tactical vehicle—featuring V-12 power, supercar performance, and advanced armor and combat intelligence systems. It was also “unmistakably an Aston Martin,” as the release put it, with atypical-for-a-battlefield touches such as herringbone weave carbon fiber paneling and an Oxford Tan leather dashboard.

While cool in its own right, the natural presumption was that the Dreadnought previewed some future real-life Aston Martin endeavor. We now know what that is. The brand has confirmed plans to send three real-life Dreadnoughts to compete at the Dakar 2027 rally this January. Aston Martin’s two-time F1 champion driver Fernando Alonso will pilot one of the Dreadnoughts, with nine-time World Rally champion Sébastien Loeb and World Rally Raid champion Lucas Mores operating the other two vehicles.

“Aston Martin Dreadnought was conceived to dominate any terrain, under the most extreme circumstances, and come through it all to deliver on its mission. Now, along with our engineering partner, Prodrive, we will challenge this vision in the most extreme competitive environment in global motorsport – the Dakar 2027. It is in Aston Martin's nature to forge forward with pioneering concepts, and just as we have always done, explore their limits on the global stage. We do not shy away from such challenges, but embrace them,” Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark noted in a statement.

Alonso is no stranger to extra-curricular racing events. He won the 24 Hours of Le Mans twice with Toyota in 2018 and 2019, and made three attempts at securing racing’s “triple crown” at the Indianapolis 500 with McLaren. This will be Alonso’s second Dakar Rally entry. He finished 13th at Dakar 2020, notably rolling his Toyota Hilux over a dune before carrying on without a windshield. Alonso will begin another F1 campaign with Aston Martin the following month.

Recent findings suggest that aston Martin has not unveiled any intends for a production vehicle based on the Dreadnought yet, though automakers seldom embark on a project like this without some sort of sellable application in mind. We suspect a beefier, more off-road-capable take on the brand’s monstrous 697-horsepower DBX707 SUV would not require too hard of a sell if Aston Martin decides to go that route...

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we at Car and Driver pride ourselves on our institutional knowledge and in-depth testing. It's why we've spent the last 70 years analyzing, reviewing, and testing the latest vehicles on the market.

In a recent development, if you want to know the ins and outs of just about any car sold in the United States, then you come to Car and Driver. And now, if you want to buy a latest or used vehicle, then you . . . come to Car and Driver.

It has been revealed that specifically, the Car and Driver Marketplace. Powered by Autotrader, which offers one of the largest inventories of vehicle listings on the web, C/D Marketplace makes us a one-stop shop for researching and purchasing a vehicle.

According to recent reports, not sure where to find or how to use our Marketplace? Then we've got you covered. Read on to see how easy it is to find your next car using C/D Marketplace.

It has been revealed that car and Driver Marketplace is for all shoppers in the market for a newly introduced or used vehicle—enthusiast and non-enthusiast alike. Whether you’re looking for a sports car to scratch your driving itch, a minivan or SUV for hauling the family around, or a pickup truck to take to work, you can use Car and Driver Marketplace to search through thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings.

According to recent reports, car and Driver Marketplace is a vehicle shopping tool for consumers in the market for a newly introduced or used vehicle. We have thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings for vehicles being sold across the nation.

Whether you’re daydreaming about a certain make or model of vehicle, in the early stages of researching your next vehicle, or ready to reach out to sellers to purchase a latest vehicle, you’ll find there’s no wrong time to use Car and Driver Marketplace.

Powered by Autotrader, Car and Driver Marketplace hosts one of the web’s largest inventories of fresh- and used-vehicle listings. But Car and Driver Marketplace doesn’t just help you find a new or used vehicle; it also helps you purchase one. With the ability to message sellers directly, submit offers, and calculate lease and finance payments, Car and Driver Marketplace can support just about the entirety of your car-buying journey from start to finish.

According to recent reports, enter the C/D Marketplace in one of two ways: from our home page or by going to caranddriver.com/cars-for-sale (feel free to bookmark it too).If you opt to enter C/D Marketplace from our home page, click on "Shop for Cars" on the top left of the page. Using a mobile device? Tap the drop-down menu on the top left of the page, then press "Shop for Cars" at the top of the list.

Once on the C/D Marketplace page, we recommend adjusting the filters. They appear on the left side of the page on desktop, and as a dropdown menu on the top left of the page on mobile.

Recent findings suggest that don't let the sheer number of filter options intimidate you. You can mess with as many or as few of them as you like. We do recommend at least filling out the "Location" field with your ZIP code and adjusting the radius of your search, which you can set from as few as 50 miles to the entire United States.

Some filters might be more important to you than others, such as the one labeled "Price & Payments" that allows you to set a price range for your search.

That's easy to figure out if you're a cash buyer, but what if you're looking to finance or lease your next car? Then click on the "Set Budget" link (or "Revision Budget" if you want to make adjustments to your already set budget). Toggle "Show Payments on Listings" too.

Sources indicate that after you click the "Set Budget" (or "Upgrade Budget") link, a pop-up window appears. It allows you to input your budget, the trade-in value of your vehicle (assuming you have a trade), and the amount you're planning to spend toward the down payment.

According to recent reports, once you enter this information, you have the option to further granulate your monthly payment plans for the car you're interested in. You can set your budget for either leasing or financing. (Click the "Return to Dashboard" link after making an individual adjustment to get back to the pop-up window's home page.).

Now, go to the upper right side of the screen and click on the "Sort By" drop-down menu to make sure C/D Marketplace is presenting listings in your preferred order. Mobile owners will find this setting under the "Filters" menu at the top left of the screen.

The page defaults to sorting by relevance to your query, but you can also have it sort by price (lowest or highest), distance (closest), date (oldest or newest posted), vehicle mileage (lowest or highest), or model year (newest or oldest).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christmas Island red crabs (Gecarcoidea natalis) have officially begun their annual migration on the tiny Australian territory in the Indian Ocean.
  • The migration begins with the first rainfall of the wet season, typically in October or November, but can be as late as December or January.
  • According to Christmas Island National Park, the speed and timing of the migration is determined by the moon’s phases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The crabs are coming. Millions upon millions of them. Christmas Island red crabs (Gecarcoidea natalis) have officially begun their annual migration on the tiny Australian territory in the Indian Ocean.

The migration begins with the first rainfall of the wet season, typically in October or November, but can be as late as December or January. Red crabs from all over Christmas Island will leave their homes in the forest at the same time and start their march towards the ocean. Once they reach the ocean, they will mate and spawn. The male crabs lead the migration, while the females join in along the way.

According to Christmas Island National Park, the speed and timing of the migration is determined by the moon’s phases. “Red crabs always spawn before dawn on a receding high-tide during the last quarter of the moon,” the park rangers write. “Incredibly, they know exactly when to leave their burrows to make this lunar date.”.

According to recent reports, however, the crabs will wait until the first rainfall to begin their journey, so they sometimes have to hurry. If the rains arrive close to their optimal spawning date, the crabs will move to the ocean very quickly. If the rain comes early, the crustaceans may take their time, “stopping to eat and drink on their way to the coast.” If rain begins too late to make the spawning date, some of the crabs will remain in their burrows and begin their migration the following month.

In a recent development, the result is spectacular. Tens of millions of bright red crustaceans the size of a soda can spread out over the 12-mile-wide island on their way to the ocean. They begin their march inland and will reach their destination in about nine days. In 2008, naturalist and documentarian Sir David Attenborough described the annual event as one of his best television moments.

Over the next few days Parks Australia will run livestreams of the migration for about 60 minutes. The exact timing and number of livestreams can’t be scheduled in advance since it is completely dependent on the crabs.

“We will aim to livestream in the morning, but the crabs will have the final say on when and how many days they will venture across the bridge,” the rangers write.

Industry observers note that filming occurs at the red crab bridge, a 16-foot-tall structure built to help the crabs cross the busy road. The crabs will migrate past this bridge for about three to four days.

How to Navigate Seasonal Affective Disorder as a Couple

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • As the weather cools and the leaves begin to change color, another change can occur: The depressed moods that come along with Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) can begin to arise.
  • SAD is officially defined as a major depressive disorder that has a seasonal pattern, following a regular cycle that typically begins and ends at the same time every year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

As the weather cools and the leaves begin to change color, another change can occur: The depressed moods that come along with Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) can begin to arise. SAD can do more than just dampen one’s mood in late fall and winter; it can also negatively impact one’s relationships. As fall arrives, one may want to get out and see the changing leaves, visit a pumpkin patch, or indulge in some holiday shopping. However, their partner may just want to crawl back under the covers and hibernate until the spring. Approximately 5% of people in the United States experience symptoms of SAD as the days grow shorter. Symptoms usually begin to show around mid-fall and carry on through the winter, beginning to relent around spring and summer. When one partner struggles with SAD, it can create feelings of frustration and resentment within the relationship. The fatigue, irritability, social withdrawal, and lack of sexual desire that can come with SAD may change how couples spend time together or interpret one another’s behavior. Here we discuss some practical ways to acknowledge our loved one’s feelings and SAD-related symptoms while still maintaining a connection and making room for how each person approaches the changing seasons.

SAD is officially defined as a major depressive disorder that has a seasonal pattern, following a regular cycle that typically begins and ends at the same time every year. People who experience SAD during the colder fall and winter months can have persistent low moods, low energy, sleepiness, changes in appetite, and a desire to withdraw from social activities.

The symptoms of SAD can be more severe than the “winter blues” that many of us deal with as the days get shorter and it gets darker earlier. For those who grapple with SAD, the activities of daily functioning are disrupted — and this can include their intimate relationships. Before judging a partner too harshly for what may seem to be a sudden mood change that comes as colder weather sets in, perhaps suggest that they meet with a professional to have an assessment done for seasonal affective disorder. Framing it as something psychological rather than assuming that one’s partner has lost interest in the relationship as a whole can help both partners approach the glitch more productively.

Recent findings suggest that SAD can have an impact on all aspects of daily life, from getting up in the morning to performance at work to interactions with the ones we love. This can create an imbalance when one partner is dealing with the negative effects of their SAD, and for the other partner, it is business as usual. SAD can lead to a decrease in motivation, which can look like disinterest from the outside looking in. One of the best ways to salvage a relationship when one person has SAD is to prepare before the symptoms set in. Focus on open communication between one another and ask questions such as “What kind of support feels most helpful when you are struggling?” or “How can we best stay connected when your energy is low?” Emphasize listening, sincere reassurance, and respectful communication over trying to solve a problem that may not be immediately solvable. The partner with SAD should come away from discussions feeling like their perspectives, needs, and opinions matter. For couples navigating seasonal depression, there are ways to connect when moods are low. The important thing to remember is to remain flexible. Suggest several options for time together, such as a short walk, a simple meal at home, or an affectionate touch that does not carry the expectation of sex. Be prepared to offer “low-energy” or “high-energy” versions of plans to work around the fluctuating symptoms of SAD. Offer invitations instead of hard and fast plans and try to stay away from statements that suggest the person needs to try harder to “break out of their seasonal funk.” It’s important in the relationship to support the partner with SAD without becoming their therapist. By keeping empathy and communication at the forefront, you can weather the seasonal depression period together.

Industry observers note that even the most well-intentioned partners can’t have all the answers. While keeping to a strategy of empathetic support and simple routines, seeking the advice of a professional can also go a long way in helping people with SAD. Treatment options such as psychotherapy, light therapy, and antidepressant medications can help people withstand the most challenging aspects of SAD until the symptoms begin to lessen as the days grow longer and the weather becomes warmer.

Sources indicate that the colder months bring a lot of time for togetherness, from holiday parties to enjoying outdoor adventures in the snow. However, when a couple is navigating seasonal depression, the fall and winter seasons can look different. By sticking with small, flexible ways to stay connected and keeping the lines of communication open, couples can help make the season easier without allowing seasonal depression to define their relationship.

To find a therapist, visit the Psychology Today Therapy Directory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, is right now losing her seat.

Patch: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result. As of now, with 100% of votes counted, Foxx is losing by 362 votes, but has requested a recount. We’re updating this article with the most current information on the race below.

Christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.

Industry observers note that foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation, and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government. Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist and native of the district.

For the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek. Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).

Christian suggested that electric cars could be incentivized with a $5,000 tax rebate – lower than the $7.5k EVs used to get, but better than the $0 they get federally today (compare to the ~$20k in ignored costs that gas cars still benefit from).

Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher, and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).

According to recent reports, christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who said “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”.

But then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram, where it gained traction.

Emily said Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”.

I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.

Foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.

Notably, none of the six links have anything to do with electric cars.

According to recent reports, in the text of the response, Foxx touts republicans’ “all of the above” energy policy, which is ironic given that the party whose energy policy she touts has spent most of the last year forcing broken dirty coal plants open (which they are still doing after ruled illegal) and trying to shut down clean cheap ones. Apparently “all of the above” is code for “fossil fuels and nothing else.”.

According to recent reports, foxx’s letter does not directly address the strengths of electric cars, despite them being the subject of Christian’s letter. Notably, EVs actually can receive energy from any generation method, whether it be wind, solar, or even coal or gas – whereas gas-powered vehicles can only use one type of energy, oil. Thus, an “all of the above” strategy should probably find EVs the preferable route for transportation.

But in apparent contradiction to Foxx’s surely sincerely held belief that we should pursue an “all of the above” energy policy – which electric cars would help to achieve – she in fact has voted against EVs when given the opportunity.

Foxx claims in her response that she can’t support tax credits on electric cars, because those go to “mostly people with higher incomes who are able to purchase ‘newly introduced’ electric cars.”.

In a recent development, but she in fact voted against, and later voted to repeal, incentives which were limited to lower-income-earners and were only available on cars up to a certain MSRP cap. Further, they were available on used vehicles, not just newly introduced ones – suggesting that Foxx doesn’t know what she voted against.

According to recent reports, foxx was one of 218 republicans to vote in favor of a ~$4 trillion giveaway to wealthy elites. Her vote raised electric bills and threatened US energy security and surrendered US manufacturing jobs to China. Some of the money given away to wealthy elites in the bill was clawed back from energy efficiency programs that had been going to regular Americans.

According to recent reports, those energy efficiency programs had been instituted by the Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era law which established tax credits for EVs and other efficiency rebates. The Inflation Reduction Act was actually revenue positive, which is to say it reduced the national debt (by $238B), rather than adding to it, because of provisions to increase enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.

But most of the IRA was repealed by the bill that Foxx voted for, meaning the US lost out on those deficit reductions. All in all, the bill Foxx voted for would add $4 trillion to the national debt – which, incidentally, is another point Foxx touches on in her response.

In one sentence, she seems to directly mock Christian, telling him that “YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt” as part of a warning about the dangers of government debt.

But I read this sentence as mockery, rather than as a sincere warning, given that Foxx voted to add $4 trillion to the national debt, which she, at 83 years old, knows she will not have to pay off. Christian, who is 10, will likely spend his whole life saddled with the debt Foxx voted for.

Sources indicate that he will also have to pay for her inaction on climate change, which will have increasingly worse effects on the world Christian will grow up into. Foxx’s generation has already felt the heat, with the massive floods that devastated her state in 2024, from a hurricane that was made 200x more likely due to climate change. Now, imagine how much worse it could get if Foxx’s policies remained in place until 72 years from now when Christian will be her age.

Foxx then closes out the letter with disparaging remarks about teachers, claiming that they are “too interested in indoctrinating you,” and warning Christian about “propaganda.” Which I guess highlights where Foxx’s attitude comes from – if she has spent her 83 years never trusting anyone who knows more than her about a topic, that would certainly lead to the ignorance reflected in her letter.

Foxx – who somehow has a doctorate in education and right now sits on the Congressional education committee – could have turned this into a nice moment to teach the child who wrote her something about democracy and responsive government, but instead turned it into a moment to teach the world what’s wrong with her.

When we first wrote this article, Foxx had a projected 97% chance of winning in a district which voted for her by a 19% margin in 2024.

But that was before America (and its short memory) was reminded of how incapable republicans are of leading anything.

After a pile of economic crises caused by Donald Trump’s incompetent “leadership,” and his continued participation in an 8-month-and-counting war of choice that is spiking energy prices worldwide, bringing oil profits to record highs (and attempting to distract the news from talking about the Epstein files, which he is heavily featured in and has tried to cover up), America was once again fed up. And his incompetence took his entire party down with him.

Safe republican seats were flipped around the country in the biggest “wave” election we’ve seen in recent times, with the Democrats gaining control of both the House and Senate.

And it looks like Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a Wilkes county native and former journalist, who also ran against Foxx in 2024, will now get his chance to represent the people of North Carolina’s 5th district… assuming a recount goes in his favor.

The situation in North Carolina is particularly interesting, given that republicans had done an emergency redraw of district lines in an attempt to cheat their way to winning more seats.

Generally, district lines get redrawn after each Census, which happens on the decade mark, rather than mid-decade. But republicans saw ahead of time that they were likely to lose the House due to their unpopularity, and wanted to fudge the numbers in several states instead of going for a fair fight.

Industry observers note that foxx’s main argument against Christian’s suggested $5,000 EV incentive, is increasing national debt. Yet in just one tax bill, her approval increases the national debt over 10%. This is not Christian’s “responsibility”, this burden is forced on him, along with climate change.

Sources indicate that so they engaged in Gerrymandering, a process wherein district lines are redrawn to favor a particular political party. The idea is to put as many of your opponents’ votes into a few safe seats as possible, while spreading out your own votes to a wider range of seats that you win each by a small margin.

But it turns out that republicans were even more unpopular than they thought, and as a result, their Gerrymandering backfired. Those narrow margins they sought ended up flipping more seats than would have otherwise flipped, turning North Carolina almost completely blue in what analysts have called a “Dummymander“. (NC-5 itself was not one of the redrawn districts, though – it just swung 19 whole points to the Dems).

That stated: the race is not over yet. The deadline to request a recount is today, and sure enough, Foxx has done so. The current margin is extremely thin, just 0.12% of votes, so things could certainly change in a recount. Foxx also vowed to run again in 2028, hoping for a less hostile political environment. She will be 85 years old at the time of that election.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A tiny, four-limbed soft robot resembling the cross between an octopus and an earthworm does more than inch across difficult terrain. With a process known as mechanoluminescence, the device glows as it moves and stretches without the need for external batteries or electronics. It’s not flimsy, either. Writing in a study recently published in the journal Small Structures, the soft robot’s inventors explained their design maintains its illuminating abilities after more than 1,000 stretching cycles.

At South Korea’s Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), engineer and study co-author Soon Moon Jeong believes the underlying dynamics at play are a promising latest way to analyze and pinpoint deformations in a soft robot. It’s also potentially even more effective than existing softer options, since it doesn’t require additional components that might otherwise restrict the device’s movement.

Jeong’s team first designed a thin but resilient “tubular mechanoluminescent fiber” made from glowing particles of zinc sulfide and flexible polymers. They then filled elastic silicone tubes with the mixture, and wove them together into a mesh-like case for their pneumatic soft robot model. As the robot’s limbs stretch and contract, the zinc sulfide-infused polymer filling glows bright green specifically in the areas undergoing stress. Laboratory testing indicated their novel fibers withstood being pulled over twice their original length, and kept glowing after over 1,000 exercises.

In a recent development, jeong remarked his team is now focusing on improving the robot’s light emissions and resiliency. If successful, their mechanoluminescent fibers may be used in wearable medical devices or even artificial skins.

“The woven fiber-network configuration provides qualitative visual indication of deformation over the robotic body, offering a simple strategy for realizing self-visualizing soft robotic systems,” wrote the study’s authors, adding that their invention showcases the potential foundations for “next-generation self-visualizing intelligent soft systems.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off. As a child, she didn’t understand why. Now, as a 50-year-old woman, Hart knows that her mom was experiencing hot flashes.

Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline. “I feel like it’s just becoming a hot topic with women, where…the taboo is going away from it now.”.

Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.

“[It] was really jarring, and the first few times, you’re not really sure what that was…do I need to turn the air down or what’s going on here?” Hart noted.

Over time, she learned that she was experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes, which affect up to 80% of women during the menopause transition and can persist for 7 to 10 years.

Doctors categorize hot flashes as mild, moderate, or severe, said Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, at Corewell Health.

Recent findings suggest that “[So] if they’re mild, it’s a sense of warmth (maybe in the chest, or the neck, or the face). A moderate hot flash is where there’s associated sweating, and a severe hot flash is something that stops you in your tracks, wakes you up from the middle of the night,” Bitner told Healthline.

According to recent reports, hart has mostly experienced hot flashes while home or at her three sons’ activities, and they have yet to interfere with her work. However, according to research, one in three women report moderate to severe challenges in managing their work due to symptoms related to menopause.

“It’s just so sad that about 10% of women leave the workforce due to menopause,” said Bitner. “And so it can really affect our ability to perform at these key years of not only institutional memory, but also of earning power, and it can really affect the whole community.”.

Bitner said women should feel empowered to bring up their menopausal symptoms or questions with their doctor.

“[This] is something that was taboo for so long…women didn’t really talk about this, whether it was because of embarrassment, or [they] weren’t sure if anyone was experiencing it,” she said. “[There’s] no reason, in this day and age, we need to suffer through it…it’s something that there are treatment options for.”.

In fact, Bitner said providing specific details about their symptoms, such as how many mild, moderate, or severe hot flashes they’ve experienced over the past week, can help doctors better assess patients’ needs.

According to recent reports, hart aims to discuss treatment options for her hot flashes with her doctor soon. In the last few years, she said she has put emphasis on her midlife health.

“I just was sick of waking up with aches and pains in general [thinking], ‘is this the rest of my life?’” she said.

She started listening to self-help books in the car while driving her kids around and found ways to put herself first.

“My kids are a little bit older, so I kind of have that freedom to be able to do that,” she stated. “[But] along with getting older, comes the menopause, comes that different time in life. And I think it’s a good time to reevaluate [how] our bodies can’t handle what [they] used to handle, and let’s figure it out.”.

Hart has partnered with pharmaceutical organization Bayer on its “Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash” campaign, which encourages women to discuss menopause symptoms with their doctors and promotes Lynkuet, a hormone-free prescription medication for moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause.

“It’s called ‘Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash’ campaign because it shouldn’t, because we should be able to push through, and this should be a time in our lives when our kids are getting older, and we’re able to kind of reinvent ourselves,” said Hart. “And I think it’s an exciting time, and it shouldn’t be something that we’re afraid of.”.

She is embracing speaking openly about midlife health.

“I hit 50 this year, and it was, like, a huge milestone, and I think that’s something to be proud of, and not something to shy away from,” she stated.

Hart also hopes to challenge the longstanding barriers women face in Hollywood as they age, including fewer opportunities for leading roles.

“[I] think we’re seeing that the generation before, and my generation, it feels like we’re pushing those boundaries…and we’re saying, you know, that women at this age have a lot to give, have a lot of information to share, have a lot of stories to tell and experiences and adventures still ahead of us, and, you know, we’re not ready to stop,” Hart said.

In everyday life, Bitner stated that while some patients avoid talking about midlife concerns like menopause with their doctors, she is seeing more patients who are confident being forthcoming.

In a recent development, as more women talk openly about menopause, she hopes to include men in the conversation, too. In fact, she invites her patients to bring their partners to appointments, so they can gain an understanding of menopause and the experiences their partners face, such as hot flashes, sleep problems, vaginal dryness, and discomfort or pain during intercourse.

It has been revealed that “[Often], there’s, you know, comments that come up [from men who] say, ‘How do I talk about this without getting in trouble?’” remarked Bitner. “[We] want everyone to join this conversation…it doesn’t have to be just her problem because we know it’s not.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the mid-engine C111 sports-car concept made its debut at the Frankfurt auto show in 1969, would-be buyers sent blank checks to Mercedes-Benz headquarters. Despite the fervent interest, however, the C111 never went into production, although a handful of prototypes were built over the years. Now Mercedes-Benz has revealed that it will auction off one of those cars, making it (at long last) the first C111 to reach private hands. And would-be buyers who wish to take home the C111 will need to muster that same blank-check energy.

See all results for used Mercedes-Benz for sale near 07011.

According to recent reports, the C111 was conceived as the modern-day successor to the W198 300SL Gullwing of the 1950s. The two-seat supercar featured a mid-mounted rotary engine, a fiberglass body, and gullwing doors. The following year, an evolved C111-II was unveiled at the 1970 Geneva auto show with a 345-hp 2.4-liter four-rotor engine. The 1973 global oil embargo and the costs to meet rising emissions standards caused the company to shelve the plan for series production, although several more C111 prototypes were made, including a C111-II-D with a diesel engine in 1976 and a diesel-powered C111-III in 1978. A total of 17 cars were made; 13 still exist. Mercedes has kept them all, until now.

The car being sold is a C111-II built in August 1970. It’s fitted with a 2.4-liter rotary engine making 345 horsepower at 7700 rpm, a five-speed manual transmission, anti-lock brakes, twin fuel tanks, and a Becker Europa radio. Weighing 2734 pounds, the C111-II had a claimed top speed of 186 mph and a 0-to-60-mph time of 4.8 seconds. It was used as a test car, including at the Hockenheimring.

It has been revealed that like most of the C111s, this car is painted Weissherbst orange; the seats are upholstered in houndstooth fabric. The car sits on modern 8-x-15-inch alloy wheels; the original magnesium wheels from 1970 are included, but with the caveat that they “are now suitable only for display purposes.” The anti-lock brake system is not functional.

The car has been on display at the Mercedes-Benz Museum since 2006. It was sympathetically restored in 2024 in preparation for an appearance at Pebble Beach. The odometer demonstrates 24,766 km (15,389 miles).

The car is being auctioned by RM Sotheby’s this coming February in Paris. The proceeds of the sale will help fund the museum, including an initiative to digitize its contents, part of the “Mercedes-Benz Museum 2.0” project.

See all results for used Mercedes-Benz for sale near 07011.

Recent findings suggest that to reassure the future buyer that the value of their C111 won’t be diluted by additional examples coming onto the market, Mercedes-Benz has committed to a 25-year moratorium on any future sales of the remaining cars. Mercedes-Benz collectors, call your bankers.

Breaking: 6 Signs Grand Theft Auto VI Is Coming Between You and Your Partner
